# Muse Fanqie download tools

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

`fanqie_search` searches the official books tab by title or keyword. Pass `query`; to continue the same search, pass the returned `nextPassback` unchanged as `passback` when `hasMore` is true. Results contain decimal string `bookId`, current and original titles, author, official page URL and declared chapter count. Match the user's title and author before passing a candidate ID to `fanqie_download`; ambiguous same-name books require selection, and search ranking does not identify the intended book. An empty result is a successful search with no candidates. Search neither writes files nor establishes download availability or completeness.

`fanqie_download_info` checks the official complete directory for one or more books. `fanqie_download` downloads all currently published chapters into UTF-8 TXT files in the initiating session workspace. Pass decimal string IDs or official `https://fanqienovel.com/page/<book-id>` links in `bookIds`. The result includes the current official title, declared and downloaded chapter counts, absolute file paths, SHA-256 and per-chapter receipts. For an ongoing book, `complete` means its current published directory; it does not mean the author has finished the novel. Directory inspection alone never claims a verified download.

The independent local Python engine uses normal anonymous device registration and read endpoints. Devices and negotiated keys stay in memory and are not copied from the reference application, published or logged. The closed-source reference application is not shipped. MIT-licensed protocol primitives retain their notices and pinned source records in `SOURCE.json`. The engine refuses paid/VIP or other authorization-required content, missing or mismatched chapters, previews, undecoded font characters and undersized text. Every book must pass before the batch directory is published; a failure or cancellation removes all newly staged files and preserves existing downloads.

Chapter extraction prefers `<article>` text when present and otherwise uses `<body>` text. It excludes `<head>`, `<script>` and `<style>` content and preserves block and `<br>` line breaks; text outside the selected container cannot satisfy the declared chapter length.

Desktop presets mount the tools and reuse the packaged Hongguo Python/PyCryptodome runtime. No additional Java service, external downloader or TOS credential is needed. An independent profile can install the package and apply `cordis.patch.yml` with `MUSE_FANQIE_PYTHON_PATH`, or configure `pythonExecutable` directly. Python must include PyCryptodome and a functioning TLS certificate store. Unconfigured runtime fails at the first call. Loading the plugin performs no network request. The Host launches isolated Python with `-X utf8`, so JSON input and output use UTF-8 on Windows and macOS regardless of the console code page. Model tools use the Host subprocess service; unload aborts and waits for active engines and cleanup.

Configuration accepts `pythonExecutable` (empty by default), `networkMode` (`direct` by default; accepts `direct` or `system`), `requestTimeoutMs` (30000), `callTimeoutMs` (1800000), `graceMs` (1000), `maxBooks` (10), `batchSize` (10), `maxResponseBytes` (16 MiB), `maxChapterBytes` (2 MiB), `maxBookBytes` (128 MiB), and `maxOutputBytes` (16 MiB). Numeric limits must be positive safe integers. There is no chapter-count cap. `outputDir` defaults to `downloads/fanqie` and must stay inside the session workspace without symlink directories. Each successful batch receives a new directory and never overwrites an older book. HTTP redirects are refused; the engine contacts only its fixed official registration and reading hosts.

`networkMode: direct` disables proxy discovery for this engine, including environment proxy variables and macOS system proxies. `networkMode: system` uses Python urllib proxy discovery from the environment and operating system. The engine never switches modes after a failure and keeps TLS certificate verification enabled in both modes. To retain system proxy behavior, apply a patch after the bundle row:

```yaml
- id: muse-fanqie-download
  config:
    pythonExecutable: !!js process.env.MUSE_FANQIE_PYTHON_PATH || process.env.MUSE_HONGGUO_PYTHON_PATH || ''
    networkMode: system
```

A patch replaces the row's complete `config`; retain any custom Python path and limits in that mapping. The example requires a Python path in one of the named environment variables. Restart the profile after applying the patch. Network mode is plugin configuration, not a model-selected tool argument.

Failed requests return `sourceStage` (`registration`, `search`, `catalog`, `key-negotiation` or `chapter-download`), the fixed destination `host`, `networkMode`, and `error` with `type`, `reasonType`, a bounded diagnostic `message`, and available `httpStatus` or `errno`. Failures before engine initialization have no request stage or host. Diagnostics omit request URLs and query strings, headers, response bodies, device identities, signing material and credentials. Muse can distinguish a registration failure from a later reading failure without exposing private protocol data. A successful catalog remains directory evidence; only successful download counts, per-chapter receipts and the TXT SHA-256 establish a complete download.

Run `node --test tests/*.test.js` and `<python> -I -B tests/engine_test.py` for offline behavior checks. `node scripts/pack.mjs --out <absolute-directory>` creates the npm archive. With the Host and native addon built, set `MUSE_FANQIE_PYTHON_PATH` to the Python path, then run `node --test tests/live.test.js` for real-source qualification. `MUSE_FANQIE_LIVE_QUERY` enables title search, catalog resolution and pagination checks; `MUSE_FANQIE_LIVE_BOOK_IDS` enables complete downloads of comma-separated authorized free-book IDs. Each case skips unless explicitly enabled. Platform package validation belongs to the final Muse release; a source-level download check does not establish that a Windows or Mac installer works.
